Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal has reiterated his administration’s firm stance against negotiating with the bandits terrorising the state.
On Thursday, the governor attended the graduation ceremony for the Zamfara Forest Guards at Government Secondary School, Gada Biyu, in Gusau.
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu launched the armed forest guard initiative on 24 May 2025 to train residents to protect forests and other ungoverned areas nationwide.
More than 1,000 forest guards in Zamfara received training in weapons handling, physical fitness, combat readiness, civil-military relations, security cooperation, community engagement, and the rule of law.
At the event, Governor Lawal thanked President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the National Security Adviser for the Federal Government’s support for the Forest Guards initiative.
He commended the security agencies, the training coordinator, and the instructors for preparing the cohort for service.
He said, “To the families of our graduates, thank you for the support and encouragement you have given them.

“We must urgently reclaim Zamfara’s vast ungoverned areas, which have become safe havens for bandits, criminals and terrorists.
“This will require sustained cooperation between federal and state authorities, a reliable security presence and the restoration of public services.
“Our goal is to ensure displaced families can return safely, and communities can farm, trade and rebuild their livelihoods.”
Governor Lawal emphasised that his administration has spent substantially on state security agencies over the past three years, providing equipment, transport, surveillance and logistical support.
“We have provided over 30 Armoured Personnel Carriers, 200 pick-up operational vehicles, 20 Toyota Buffalo vehicles, more than 1,000 specialised motorcycles, and additional vehicles and motorcycles for the Homegrown Community Protection Guards.
“We have also supplied surveillance drones, including an 80-metre endurance model that covers up to 50 kilometres and operates continuously for eight hours, improving reconnaissance, situational awareness and coordination in difficult terrain.
“I want to make it clear again, we are still firm in our decision never to negotiate with the criminals terrorising our state.”
